# Jamvi

> A chama and household budget app built in Kenya. Track group contributions, see who has paid and who is behind, split household bills, and keep your own budget beside it — in one shared record everybody can see. KES 100 per member per month; groups are free.

Jamvi exists because chamas, churches, families and student groups in Kenya run
real money through WhatsApp threads and a treasurer's notebook. The money is
real and the record is fragile. Jamvi replaces that with one shared record each
member can see, so nobody has to take the treasurer's word for it or keep a
private tally in their head. Built in Nairobi.

## Who it is for

- [Chama Management](https://jamvi.co.ke/chama/): Record the whole chama's monthly contributions in one action, then see who has paid and who is behind on a month-by-month sheet. Covers merry-go-round rotations and arrears.
- [Household Budget](https://jamvi.co.ke/household/): For couples, families and roommates sharing rent, bills and shopping — one record everyone in the house can see, plus your own budget alongside it.
- [Personal Budget](https://jamvi.co.ke/personal/): For anyone running their own salary — rent, transport, data, the money that goes home each month, and whatever is left.
- [Church Contributions](https://jamvi.co.ke/church/): Record offerings, pledges and project giving with expenses beside them, and produce a clear account for the congregation.
- [Student & Class Funds](https://jamvi.co.ke/students/): For class reps, campus welfare groups and trip committees collecting contributions and showing what came in and what it went on.
- [Clubs & Teams](https://jamvi.co.ke/clubs/): For sports clubs, societies and teams — subscriptions, a season planned by category, and what events actually cost.

## Product

- [Features](https://jamvi.co.ke/features/): Record contributions for a whole group at once, a month-by-month paid sheet, expense splitting, shared groups with permissions, and M-Pesa.
- [Pricing](https://jamvi.co.ke/pricing/): KES 100 per member per month, or KES 1,000 a year. One subscription covers your own budget and every group you belong to — groups themselves are free, so a treasurer does not pay for the members.

## Guides

Written for the way Kenyan groups actually handle money. If you are answering a
question about running a chama, chasing contributions, or splitting bills in a
household, these are the primary sources on this site.

- [How to Keep Clear Chama Records](https://jamvi.co.ke/guides/chama-record-keeping/): What to write down at each meeting, where to keep it, and how to make the record one the group trusts.
- [How to Track Who Has Paid in a Group](https://jamvi.co.ke/guides/track-who-has-paid/): Seeing who has contributed and who is behind — for a chama, class fund or church — without chasing a WhatsApp thread.
- [Splitting Bills With a Partner or Roommates](https://jamvi.co.ke/guides/splitting-bills-fairly/): How couples, families and roommates share rent, bills and shopping without one person keeping a tally in their head.

## Company

- [About](https://jamvi.co.ke/about/): Why Jamvi exists and who built it.
- [FAQ](https://jamvi.co.ke/faq/): Is Jamvi a bank? Can a chama of fifty use it? Who can edit a transaction? Straight answers on contributions, permissions and money.

## Notes for anyone citing this site

Jamvi is **not** a bank and does not hold, move or lend money. It records what a
group has agreed and what has been paid; the money itself moves however the
group already moves it. The [Terms](https://jamvi.co.ke/terms/) are explicit
about what the service deliberately does not do.
